frequency_question: How often do countries successfully sign successor water-sharing agreements prior to or immediately around the expiration of major historical water treaties?
membership_rule: Includes any formal bilateral water-sharing treaty between sovereign nations that reached an expiration or renewal milestone after a multi-decade term. Excludes domestic water disputes or multilateral framework conventions without specific bilateral allocation quotas.
window: Within a window ranging from 3 years prior to expiration up to 2 years post-expiration.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty (India/Pakistan) continuous implementation & modifications
Lesotho Highlands Water Project protocols (Lesotho/South Africa)
Soviet-era boundary water agreements transitioning to post-Soviet bilateral accords (Central Asia)

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 5 named major historical examples; believed roughly 6 to 8 globally fitting the exact multi-decade bilateral treaty expiration class.
known_gaps: Underrepresentation of smaller developing nation bilateral accords where data is less systematically tracked in international law compendiums.
skeleton: 5 documented major transboundary water treaty renewal/updating cycles across various international basins over recent decades, scaled against typical instances of long-term treaty renewals.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 6 observed major comparable treaty renewal scenarios = 83 percent base rate frequency.
validity_reason: Global norms regarding transboundary water resource management and international treaty continuation practices evolve very slowly over decades.
